questions.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
questions.problem: Given that $u=1+{x}^{2}$, which integral is equivalent to $\int \frac{{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u=1+{x}^{2}$, then we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,x\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
${x}^{2}=u-1$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}} & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}\cdot {x}^{2}\cdot x\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot (u-1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int ({u}^{1/2}-{u}^{-1/2})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $u=2x+1$, which integral is equivalent to $\int x\sqrt[3]{2x+1}\,\text{d}x?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u=2x+1$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{1}{2}(u-1).$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt[3]{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{2}(u-1)(\sqrt[3]{u})(\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int (u-1)({u}^{1/3})\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int ({u}^{4/3}-{u}^{1/3})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $u=3-2{x}^{2}$, which integral is equivalent to ${\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{3}\sqrt{3-2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u=3-2{x}^{2}$, then we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4x\,⟹\,-\frac{\text{d}u}{4}=x\text{d}x.
$$

We also note that ${x}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}(3-u).$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $-1$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $1$ | $3$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{3}\sqrt{3-2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{2}\sqrt{3-2{x}^{2}}\cdot x\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(3-u)\sqrt{u}\cdot (-\frac{\text{d}u}{4}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{1}^{3}(3-u)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating Definite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
questions.worked_solution:
Let $u=2x+1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{1}{2}(u-1).$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $-1/2$ | $3/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $0$ | $4$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/2}^{3/2}4x\sqrt{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{4}4\cdot \frac{1}{2}(u-1)\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}({u}^{3/2}-{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & ={(\frac{1}{(5/2)}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{1}{(3/2)}{u}^{3/2})|}_{0}^{4} \\  & ={(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}\cdot {4}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}\cdot {4}^{3/2})-(\frac{2}{5}\cdot {0}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}\cdot {0}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{64}{5}-\frac{16}{3} \\  & =\frac{112}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating Definite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
questions.worked_solution:
Let $u=x+3.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=u-3.$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $1$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $4$ | $9$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}\frac{3x+1}{\sqrt{x+3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{4}^{9}\frac{3(u-3)+1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{9}\frac{3u-8}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{9}(3{u}^{1/2}-8{u}^{-1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & ={(\frac{3}{(3/2)}{u}^{3/2}-\frac{8}{(1/2)}{u}^{1/2})|}_{4}^{9} \\  & ={(2{u}^{3/2}-16{u}^{1/2})|}_{4}^{9} \\  & =(2\cdot {9}^{3/2}-16\cdot {9}^{1/2})-(2\cdot {4}^{3/2}-16\cdot {4}^{1/2}) \\  & =(2\cdot 27-16\cdot 3)-(2\cdot 8-16\cdot 2) \\  & =(54-48)-(16-32) \\  & =6-(-16) \\  & =22\end{aligned}
$$
